title: Family Structure in Sarasota County, FL (2005–2024)
text:
Explore how households, families with children, and neighborhood demographics have evolved in Sarasota County and across Florida using U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) data. Hover over any chart or map below to inspect specific years, counties, and neighborhoods.

1. Twenty Years of Household Growth (Interactive Trend)
This chart tracks how Sarasota County’s households have changed from 2005 to 2024 using the U.S. Census Bureau’s 1-Year American Community Survey (Table B11001). Note that 2020 is omitted because the Census Bureau did not release standard 1-year ACS estimates that year due to COVID-19 data-collection disruptions.

What the Census categories mean: The Census divides households into family households (two or more people related by birth, marriage, or adoption living together—broken down into married couples, single-mother/female householders, and single-father/male householders) and nonfamily households (people living alone or exclusively with unrelated roommates).
Key takeaway: Over the past two decades, total households in Sarasota County grew by 36.5% (from 165,367 to 225,791) alongside a rising median age (from 49.4 to 57.6 years). Almost all of that growth was driven by married-couple families (+40%, from 83,787 to 117,233) and nonfamily households (+36%, from 63,748 to 86,665, reflecting a large retiree population living alone), while single-mother (15,332 in 2024) and single-father (6,561 in 2024) family counts grew much more slowly.









2. Florida Counties: Children per Family & Demographics (Interactive Map)
Using 5-Year ACS data (2018–2022, Tables B09001 and B11003), this map compares family size among families raising children across all 67 Florida counties, with Sarasota County outlined in red.

Why this measure matters: Sarasota County has one of the oldest populations in Florida (median age 57.1), meaning many households are retirees without children at home. Instead of dividing children by all households, this map divides the population under 18 (B09001_001) by the total number of families that actually have children under 18 (married couples plus single mothers and single fathers with children).
Key takeaway: When looking strictly at families raising kids, Sarasota County averages 2.07 children per family—very typical for Florida, where counties range from 1.56 (Glades County) to 2.94 (Gadsden County). Hovering over Sarasota also shows that 31.8% of its families with children are headed by a single parent and the county-wide median household income is $77,213.









3. Inside Sarasota County: Neighborhood Income & Family Structure
County-wide averages can hide huge differences from one neighborhood to the next. This bubble chart zooms inside Sarasota County using Census tract data (2018–2022 5-Year ACS) for every neighborhood with at least 25 families with children.

How to read the chart: Each circle is a Sarasota County Census tract. The horizontal axis shows the percentage of families with children headed by a single mother or single father, the vertical axis shows the tract’s median household income (B19013_001), the bubble size reflects the total number of families with children in that neighborhood, and the color shows the neighborhood’s median age (ranging from 32.8 to 74.2 years).
Key takeaway: There is a clear economic divide tied to family structure across Sarasota neighborhoods. Census tracts with lower shares of single-parent families tend to have substantially higher median household incomes (reaching up to $160,500), whereas neighborhoods where single parents head half or more of all families with children often have median household incomes between $35,000 and $60,000.
